thread:
claire: noticed several tenants saw token attribution move to the wrong tenant in invoice-preview after we enabled shared-batch-pool on the GPU pods. small numbers (~50-200 tokens) but consistent for requests that overlap at 09:14 UTC.
omar: explain "wrong tenant" — batching shouldn't change per-request accounting, we emit per-request token counts before batching, right?
claire: that's what we assumed. but runtime batching implementation merged decode+generation and the finalizer only looks at the batch envelope. in a few codepaths the per-request metadata was dropped when the fast-path batch packed multiple origins. gist: finalizer used batch.tokens_by_position but the map-of-req-ids got nulled for pooled batches.
jin: logs?
claire: pasted snippet: 
```
2024-09-10T09:14:11Z INFO runtime batch.start batch_id=B-42 tenants=[T-A,T-B] positions=2
2024-09-10T09:14:12Z INFO runtime batch.complete batch_id=B-42 tokens_total=300 tokens_positions=[120,180] metadata_map=null
2024-09-10T09:14:12Z INFO meter persist batch_id=B-42 owner=first_position tokens=300 persisted=true
```
so aggregator saw one event owned by first_position (T-A) with 300 tokens -> T-B lost attribution, T-A got overcharged.
omar: ouch. how did metadata_map become null? sounds like a memory optimization that elided the per-request map for pooled batches.
jin: I remember a PR that avoids allocating maps in the "single-tenant" fast path and then reused that path for multi-tenant pooling by mistake. runtime owner here.
claire: right. rollout note didn't catch it because our small-unit tests used single-tenant batches. Multi-tenant pooling only happens under high concurrency.
omar: quick mitigation: change finalizer to refuse to emit a single-owner batch event when metadata_map is null AND positions>1. Instead, it should split the batch into per-request meter events using tokens_positions. cheap to implement: 
```
if (batch.metadata_map == null && batch.positions > 1) {
  for i in positions:
    emit meter(event{tenant=positions[i].tenant, tokens=tokens_positions[i]})
  return
}
```

jin: agree. that's localized. downside: more small events persisted which might regress throughput but only for these rare pooled batches.
sara: alternative is to restore metadata_map allocation unconditionally, but that reintroduces allocations and GC pressure. prefer the split-on-null approach for safety.
ops-bot: suggested rollout: apply patch to runtime -> canary 5% of GPU pods -> monitor invoice-preview per-tenant deltas and metering throughput.
metering-bot: add metric suggestion `metering.batch_split_count` and an alert if it spikes > 1000/min during canary.
claire: will open PR with tests that simulate multi-tenant pooled batch with metadata_map null and assert correct per-tenant emits. also adding a stress test in performance suite. PR #8789.
jin: will own deploy. I'll also add a feature flag `batch.split_on_missing_metadata=true` so we can flip without full rollback.
omar: follow-up longer-term: we should change batch plumbing to always carry a compact per-request token-intent array (tenant_id + token_hint) that is cheap and GC-friendly so we never have to reconstruct on split. file a tech debt ticket.
sara: UI/Console follow-up: add a transient annotation on invoice-preview when we've split a pooled batch so CS can explain small timing artifacts. `metering.batch_split=true` and console tooltip.
claire: good idea. Also schedule a one-off reconciliation for the 12 affected tenants from today to correct the misattributed tokens. I can run a query to find events where batch.owner != sum of tokens_positions.
ops-bot: reconcile job scheduled for 2024-09-11T02:00Z UTC. will post results.
metering-bot: CANARY: runtime patch deployed to 5% canary pods. monitoring invoice-preview.
claire: can confirm preview deltas normalized on canary sample. staging will follow. closing thread when staged promoted. :thumbsup:
